candidates.angle: ajah means unborn, the first quality Krishna lists for the self
the self is ancient, existing before any body or time began
the self is not slain when the body is slain

en.intro: How do you end what has no beginning? Krishna answers with a list of what the self is not. Listen for the first word.
en.notice: The first word Krishna speaks is ajah, unborn. The self did not come into being, and it will not cease to be again. It is beyond the cycle of birth and death.
en.next: If the self is unborn, Krishna then asks what happens when the body is destroyed.
en.meaning: It is never born and never dies. It did not come into being, and it will not cease. Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.

hi.intro: जिसकी कोई शुरुआत न हो, उसे कैसे खत्म किया जा सकता है? श्रीकृष्ण बताते हैं कि आत्मा क्या नहीं है, और उसके लिए क्या शब्द हैं।
hi.meaning: यह शरीरधारी कभी जन्म नहीं लेता और न कभी मरता है तथा यह उत्पन्न होकर फिर होने वाला नहीं है। यह अजन्मा, नित्य, शाश्वत और सबसे प्राचीन अनादि है। शरीर के मारे जाने पर भी यह नहीं मारा जाता।
hi.notice: श्रीकृष्ण के मुँह से पहला शब्द है अजः, अर्थात् अजन्मा। यह कभी जन्म नहीं लेता और न कभी मरता है।
hi.next: यदि आत्मा अजन्मा है, तो श्रीकृष्ण पूछते हैं कि शरीर के नष्ट होने पर उसका क्या होता है।

issues: meaning_changed: "The first word Krishna speaks is ajah, unborn. The self did not come into being at some point, and it will not exist again after ceasing to be. It is beyond the cycle of birth and death." (The Hindi translation of the verse explicitly states 'यह उत्पन्न होकर फिर होने वाला नहीं है' (having come into being, it will not happen again/exist again) and 'नित्य' (eternal/continuous). The notice claims the self 'will not exist again after ceasing to be', which contradicts the verse's meaning that the self never comes into being and is eternal/continuous.)

meaning_changed: "The first word Krishna speaks is ajah, unborn. The self never came into being at some point, and it will not come into being again because it is eternal and continuous." (The English notice adds the phrase 'at some point' and 'again because it is eternal and continuous', which are interpretive additions not strictly supported by the source verse's direct meaning. The source emphasizes it never came into being and will not cease, but the notice frames it as a temporal 'point' and a causal 'because', slightly altering the precise philosophical meaning.)

meaning_changed: "श्रीकृष्ण के मुँह से पहला शब्द है अजः, अर्थात् अजन्मा। यह कभी पैदा नहीं हुआ और न ही कभी खत्म होगा क्योंकि यह नित्य और शाश्वत है।" (The Hindi notice adds the word 'कभी' (ever/at any time) in 'कभी पैदा नहीं हुआ' and 'कभी खत्म होगा', and adds 'क्योंकि यह नित्य और शाश्वत है' (because it is eternal and everlasting), which are interpretive additions not strictly supported by the source verse's direct meaning.)

meaning_changed: "यह उत्पन्न होकर फिर होने वाला नहीं है" (The source says the self did not come into being and will not cease to be again (न भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः). The Hindi phrase 'उत्पन्न होकर फिर होने वाला नहीं है' incorrectly implies that the self was born once and then does not happen again, which contradicts the source meaning.)

borrowed: "श्रीकृष्ण पूछते हैं कि शरीर के नष्ट होने पर उसका क्या होता है" (This phrasing is borrowed from the NEXT verse's context. The current verse (20) explicitly states what happens to the self when the body is destroyed ('it is not destroyed when the body is destroyed'), rather than asking what happens.)
